title: The advantages of extended nonreciprocal quantum batteries
authors: Meng-Long Song, Zan Cao, Hai-Tao Dong, Si-Yu Zhang, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, Dong Wang
abstract: This study investigates the performance of extended nonreciprocal quantum batteries (QBs), as well as its advantages in energy storage and energy transfer compared to reciprocal charging and the original nonreciprocal batteries. After analyzing the detuning between the charging system and the external pump, we discover that resonance is a key factor in maintaining high-energy batteries and high charging power; furthermore, the detuning of the charger or battery determines the stability of the charging process for different structures. Research on steady-state energy storage in batteries revealed that single-threaded or multi-threaded charging can achieve nearly infinite energy storage in weakly localized environments, thereby demonstrating the significant energy advantages of extended nonreciprocal quantum batteries. Finally, by considering the energy distribution within the charging system, we observe that nonreciprocal charging offers energy transfer advantages unmatched by reciprocal charging; the former achieves a comprehensive balance between charging cost and energy storage capacity that the latter cannot match. As a novel and superior charging protocol, our findings are expected to provide a potent reference for the promotion and practical implementation of nonreciprocal charging.
summary: This paper analyzes extended nonreciprocal quantum batteries to optimize energy storage and transfer. It demonstrates that nonreciprocal charging protocols significantly outperform reciprocal methods by achieving higher energy storage and transfer efficiency. The findings provide a theoretical framework for implementing superior, robust charging mechanisms in quantum energy systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the performance and inherent advantages of extended nonreciprocal quantum batteries (QBs) for energy storage and energy transfer compared to standard reciprocal and original nonreciprocal charging protocols.
main_result: Extended nonreciprocal charging protocols demonstrate superior energy transfer capabilities and achieve high steady-state energy storage, particularly in multi-threaded configurations, which are unmatched by reciprocal charging.
method: The analysis uses the Lindblad quantum master equation to model system dynamics and derives maximum steady-state energy and energy transfer ratios by comparing different charging topologies.
model_or_system: The model involves an extended nonreciprocal QB system comprising chargers and a battery, described by Hamiltonians for single-threaded and multi-threaded couplings. The dynamics are governed by the Lindblad master equation.
key_observables: Stored energy ($E_{s,c}, E_{m,c}$), charging power ($P_{s,c}, P_{m,c}$), energy ratio ($\eta$), and gain function ($G$).
important_parameters: Detuning ($\Delta_i$) between the charging system and the external pump, and the dissipation ratio ($\kappa/\Gamma$).
main_assumptions: The analysis compares the extended nonreciprocal scheme against reciprocal and original nonreciprocal protocols, assuming the system can reach steady-state energy limits.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic structure of the QB, show time evolution of stored energy and power for different charging flows, and plot energy ratios and gains comparing various charging protocols.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the physical model and dynamics, then analyzing the impact of detuning on single- and multi-threaded charging, and finally quantifying the energy transfer advantages using energy ratios and gain functions.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems dynamics, specifically focusing on engineered nonreciprocal couplings to enhance energy storage and transfer, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and quantum energy harvesting.
